title: Degree-zero cohomology of a constant sheaf over a strictly henselian local ring
statement: Let $R$ be a strictly henselian local ring [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], let $X=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-pc-scheme], and let $A$ be an abelian group. For the constant étale sheaf $\underline A$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] on $X$, there is a natural additive equivalence $H^0(X_{\mathrm{Et}},\underline A)\simeq A$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology].

source.place: degree zero clause of the blueprint proof

external.place: Tag 03QO, lemma-vanishing-etale-cohomology-strictly-henselian, lines 8207–8247: sections equal the closed geometric stalk; specialize to a constant abelian sheaf.

proof.text: Apply clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-degree-zero] with T=X and G=\underline A. Its canonical additive isomorphism epsilon identifies \Gamma(X,\underline A) with H^0(X_{\mathrm{Et}},\underline A), for precisely the K-injective derived-global-sections cohomology of the statement; take its inverse. This is natural in the abelian sheaf and independent of the resolution.

source.place: Tag 05TD, lemma-left-exact-higher-derived, clause (3), specialized to global sections

proof.text: The local ring R has its proper maximal ideal \mathfrak m, giving a point of X. Every proper ideal is contained in a maximal ideal, which must be \mathfrak m; in particular every prime \mathfrak p is contained in \mathfrak m. By the Zariski definition, a closed subset V(J) contains \mathfrak p exactly when J⊆\mathfrak p, and then J⊆\mathfrak m, so V(J) also contains \mathfrak m. If X=C\amalg D is a partition into closed and open subsets, the part containing \mathfrak m must contain every point: a point in the other closed part would force \mathfrak m to belong to that part as well. Thus the other part is empty and X is connected in the nonempty sense of [def-weil-connected-scheme]. This is a direct use of the defining closed subsets V(J) in the affine spectrum [def-weil-affine-spectrum] and the local-ring hypothesis [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology].

source.place: Elementary local-spectrum argument: every prime is contained in the unique maximal ideal

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf-sections-connected] with T=X and E=A, using the connectedness just proved. It says that the canonical constant-section homomorphism iota_X:A→\underline A(X) is an additive isomorphism. Compose the inverse of epsilon from Step 1 with the inverse of iota_X to obtain H^0(X_{\mathrm{Et}},\underline A)≃A.

source.place: Tag 03P5, remark-constant-locally-constant-maps; degree-zero clause of the blueprint

proof.text: For an abelian-group homomorphism u:A→B, the constant-presheaf map sends the constant section a to u(a), and sheafification carries this to \underline u(iota_X(a))=iota_X(u(a)); the sheafified map is defined by the universal property [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] so that its composite with the sheafification unit is the unit composed with the constant-presheaf map [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Naturality of epsilon in Step 1 then gives u∘(iota_X^{-1}∘epsilon_A^{-1})=(iota_X^{-1}∘epsilon_B^{-1})∘H^0(\underline u). Both factors are additive isomorphisms, so their composite is the claimed natural additive equivalence.
